messages.subject: Hadoop Environment and HADOOP_CMD
parts:
Hello,
I am having a problem as many others, while none of the known solutions is working for me...
I have installed rhdfs with environment variables HADOOP_CMD and all. And I can manipulate files on the cluster from local machine.
But when I try loading rhdfs in the cluster(with mapreduce of a map function loading rhdfs) I get this common error that HADOOP_CMD must be set before loading package rhdfs.
 
So may I ask what is the difference between the local environment and the environment in which rmr2 runs? Is the latter the Hadoop environment that could be configured with the hadoop-conf.sh file?
I tried adding export HADOOP_CMD=... in that file but nothing happens. I still have the same error as above.
I also added export HADOOP_CMD=... in /etc/environment and it is still not working...
I tried adding export HADOOP_CMD=... in the command script and still no
I even tried this:
values(from.dfs(mapreduce(to.dfs(1), map = function(k, v){
system("export HADOOP_CMD=/usr/bin/hadoop")
Sys.getenv("HADOOP_CMD")
})))
without success
I would very much appreciate your help and advices.
 
Thanks a lot :)

messages.author: 63023c771a070260
messages.subject: Re: Hadoop Environment and HADOOP_CMD
parts:
Trying to use rhdfs in the map or reduce functions is almost always a mistake, so my first suggestion is don't do it or let's discuss your use case. Many others have problems with the installation, no discussion about that,  but your problem is unique and of your own doing. You won't find any documentation about what you are trying to do because it is wrong.  If you want to make it work anyway and don't care about performance, you can use the backend parameter cmdenv (see the documentation for hadoop streaming and help(mapreduce) in R for details) or modify a configuration file but on top of my mind it is hadoop-env.sh, not the one you mentioned. But the best way forward is to understand why you won't make your input the input to the mr job, that is the input argument to the mapreduce function and find a better approach.

Antonio

Hello Antonio,
 
thank you very much for your advices!
 
If I may, I would try to describe my case (which is rather simple...):
 
I have a huge table(10G) saved on the cluster and I want to remove certain columns in it.
So what I tried to do e.g. is:
 
map.function <- function(., dat) {
  this.dat <- dat[, -rm.cols]                                       # removing the columns
  return(keyval(1, this.dat))                                      # returning the keyval
}
 
reduce.function <- function(k, v) {
  output.file <- hdfs.file(output.path, "w")                 # creating a output file "connection"
  hdfs.write(v, output.file)                                        # writing to the connection
  hdfs.close(output.file)                                           # closing connection
  return(keyval(1, 1))                                               # returning doesn't matter 
} 
 
 
So basically I want to have the reducer write the merged tables directly to a file in HDFS instead of using output. Because while trying output I keep getting the "java.lang.OutOfMemoryError: Java Heap Space". Now I guess I should go back to the output story and set larger java heap sizes...But how big should it be?
 
Would you mind explaining to me a little more about why it is not recommended to have rhdfs running in map or reduce functions? Does that imply that I only need rhdfs on the main host?
 
Thank you very much for your answers!

parts:
On Thu, Nov 14, 2013 at 10:00 AM, Tuyki <yinchon...@gmail.com> wrote:
Hello Antonio,
 
thank you very much for your advices!
 
If I may, I would try to describe my case (which is rather simple...):
 
I have a huge table(10G) saved on the cluster and I want to remove certain columns in it.
So what I tried to do e.g. is:
 
map.function <- function(., dat) {
  this.dat <- dat[, -rm.cols]                                       # removing the columns
  return(keyval(1, this.dat))                                      # returning the keyval
}

I don't know where to start.

map.function  = function(., data) {
 dat[, -rm.cols]      }

mapreduce(input, output, map = map.function)

Done! Some comments

* you don't need a reducer to  select columns, you don't even need a key.
* you can't use a single key unless you are using a combiner, or the map  output is tiny
* you don't need to assign, return blabla unless you are a Java programmer paid by the line of boilerplate code you churn out. This is R.
* absolutely never use hdfs from inside map or reduce unless you are a master of mapreduce. You are ignoring issues of locality and concurrent writes. The system will write garbage or grind to a halt. You could do it but for smaller data sizes, for a secondary kind of output, and you absolutely need to use attempt-unique filenames.  If you don't know what a task attempt is, you are not yet a mapreduce master. Your insistence of not returning a value from the reduce function is hard to understand for me, absolutely unwarranted and I hope other readers are not tempted into trying this anti-pattern. How many times did I use rhdfs in the rmr2 tutorial? Zero. That ought to suggest something.
* the java out of memory error is probably some stuff that you are writing in stdout that confuses the java typedbytes parser. If you could show more of the stack trace I could be more confident about this. I am not sure what would cause that in your code, could be some package that you have loaded in your environment. Detach any package you don't need in the mr job to simplify things.
I hope this helps


Antonio
